items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: Herb Jeffries -- I think -- he sang it. He was the vocalist.

ctx.x: came out, (unintelligible). And then some more of the orchestra -- Duke Ellington's orchestra, you see. And he done "Prelude to a Kiss." And I think he was in the works of this song -- it never did become too popular, but it got recognition, you know. It was some kind of ballad -- yes, it did. Herb Jeffries -- I think -- he sang it. He was the vocalist. After that, then, back to the dancers, you know.

It was very classy, very classy. That's why I say rich, you know, enriching. See, Duke Ellington's appearances, you know, on these tours -- because I mean America couldn't keep this man very long -- he was in such great demand with that orchestra, see. I mean, there was other countries that wanted him on radio and so forth, make records -- recording companies, you see. And he was like in and out of America, you see. His home base was up here in the Cotton Club. Whenever he was here -- he didn't do too many…
